newsitem.title: CANADA: MacMillan halts Clayoquout logging for year.
newsitem.headline: MacMillan halts Clayoquout logging for year.

text.p: MacMillan Bloedel Ltd has halted logging in the Clayoquot Sound area of British Columbia until 1998 because of high costs and uncertainties, the Vancouver Sun newspaper reported Wednesday.
The forest company outlined its plans in a letter sent to 77 employees at its Kennedy Lake division late last month, offering severance packages and buyouts, the paper said.
A company source said the report was correct but MacMillan officials were not immediately available for comment.
Since 1993, timber harvests have fallen sharply in the Clayoquot rain forest after environmental protests prompted government cutbacks and more stringent logging rules.

"There will not be enough timber available in Clayoquot to sustain present jobs, equipment and overhead at Kennedy Lake division....It isn't merely a question of adjusting or downsizing the operation but rather of creating a completely different kind of operation," the letter to employees said, according to the report.
The article quoted a company spokesman as saying MacMillan lost C$7 million on its Clayoquot operations in 1996.
MacMillan harvested only 52,000 cubic meters of wood there in 1996 instead of a planned 100,000.

A restructured operation would harvest about 50,000 cubic meters a year after 1998, the article said. The company expects to keep its logging operation shut in area for all of 1997 and part of 1998, the newspaper said.
MacMillan is the largest forest company operating in the area. International Forest Products Ltd also has operations there.
